### **POSITION****SUMMARY:**

Working closely with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team, the Director of Program Quality and Training of Youth Programs documents best practices, designs tools to measure staff and youth outcomes, and supports collaboration among youth-serving organizations. This role provides strategic leadership for quality improvement, staff development, and outcomes assessment across Cambridge Youth Programs’ five youth centers serving more than 1,200 youth ages 9–19, partnering with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team to codify best practices, build measurement tools, and strengthen collaboration among youth-serving organizations. The Director directly supervises an Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector, and manages organization-wide partnerships, grant implementation and reporting, and recruitment and outreach efforts.

### **ESSENTIAL****JOB****FUNCTIONS****and****DUTIES:**

*The**essential**functions**or**duties**listed**below**are**intended**only**as**illustrations**of**the**various**type**of**work**that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Support expanded learning and out-of-school-time programs serving youth ages 9–19 across the City’s youth centers, including afterschool programs, evening programs, school vacation programming, and specialized youth activities.
* Assist the Division Head for Youth Programs in establishing program goals, objectives, and operational priorities.
* Assist with oversight of programs and activities across the City’s youth centers and collaborate with

 Youth Program staff as part of the Cambridge Youth Programs Leadership Team.
* Provide strategic oversight and support for program quality improvement initiatives and develop systems to assess, track, and manage program performance using positive youth development principles.
* Develop and implement systems to identify staff training and professional development needs and design and deliver training programs that support best practices in youth development, out-of-school-time programming, and effective supervision.
* Provide guidance and support to program staff in program planning, implementation, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop and manage organization-wide partnerships, initiatives, and grant partnerships, including implementation oversight and grant reporting; support recruitment materials development and outreach to prospective participants and partner organizations.
* Supervise a Youth Connector who develops and supports sites around middle school and teen transition programs, pre-teen, middle school, and teen recruitment and enrollment, and the organization’s social media plan.
* Provide direct coaching support to assigned youth center sites, working with Program Directors on a weekly basis to develop, implement, and assess both site-based plans and collective projects across the organization.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations to design and implement tools that measure staff and youth outcomes, support organizational accountability, and evaluate program effectiveness.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations, develop, coordinate, and manage staff trainings and professional development for full-time and part-time staff.
* Conduct program evaluations, analyze data, and prepare quarterly reports that support performance measurement and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop relationships with internal and external stakeholders and support collaboration and resource sharing among youth centers, schools, community organizations, families, and public safety partners.
* Perform related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Education/Experience***

* A bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a related field; master’s degree preferred.
* Three (3) years of out-of-school time (OST) program management experience required.
* Five (5) years of experience supervising staff and working with diverse populations required.
* Demonstrated knowledge of positive youth development principles and experience in program development required.
* Experience developing and implementing systems for program delivery, staff training, program quality improvement, evaluation, and assessment processes.
* Demonstrated ability to influence without direct line authority and provide leadership in developing and sustaining collaborative internal and external partnerships.
* Experience working with community agencies, youth, and schools required.
* Strong interpersonal, communication, presentation, writing, organizational, and facilitation skills required.
* An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant lived or professional experience may be considered.

***Knowledge,******Skills,******and*** ***Abilities:***
-------------------------------------------------------

* Deep knowledge of positive youth development, out-of-school time program models, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically responsive practices.
* Skill in designing, facilitating, and evaluating staff training using adult learning principles, coaching strategies, and reflective supervision techniques.
* Ability to develop and implement program quality frameworks and assessment tools and use qualitative and quantitative data to support continuous improvement efforts.
* Strong facilitation, presentation, and written communication skills, including the ability to convene diverse stakeholders and lead collaborative problem-solving initiatives across multiple sites.
* Proficiency with data management, project management, and budgeting tools and systems.
* Ability to manage complex projects, timelines, and competing priorities while ensuring compliance with applicable policies and regulations.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, and leadership skills with the ability to build and sustain collaborative partnerships.
* Commitment to anti-racism, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
* Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.

### **Works****under****the****general****direction****of****the****Division****Head****of****Cambridge****Youth****Programs;****exercises****considerable independent judgment; and has work reviewed through conferences, reports, and achievement of program** **objectives.**

### 

### **SUPERVISION****EXERCISED:**

### **May****directly****supervise****two full-time staff members:****an****Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector.****Also provides functional supervision and coaching support to Program Directors and staff across assigned youth center sites; may oversee consultants or interns engaged in training, program quality, and evaluation** **initiatives.**

### 

### **WORK** **ENVIRONMENT:**

### **Work is performed in a standard office setting with fluorescent lighting, carpeted floors, air conditioning, and moderate noise levels. Evening and weekend hours may be required to support operational needs.**

### 

### **PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:**

Ability to travel throughout the City of Cambridge to multiple Youth Center locations as required.**

**About CAMP Systems:** 
At CAMP Systems, we are the trusted leader in aircraft compliance and health management, proudly serving the global business aviation industry. With over 20,000 aircraft and 33,000 engines supported on our cutting-edge platforms, and partnerships with more than 1,300 maintenance facilities and parts suppliers worldwide, we’re shaping the future of aviation technology. Since our founding in 1968, we’ve grown to a dynamic team of 1,600+ employees across 14 locations globally—all united by a passion for innovation and excellence.

**Our Mission & Vision:** 
We connect the aviation industry through smart technology to make flight safer and more efficient, driving the future of aviation with intelligence and exceptional customer experiences.

**Our Values & Excellence Mindset:** 
We are customer obsessed, trust-driven, owners of our work, stronger together, constantly curious, and boldly innovative.

 

**What You Will Experience in This Role:**

The Director – Quality Assurance drives quality across CAMP's Aircraft Health Management business and provides quality oversight for data and process quality concerns. The role owns the QMS, the internal audit program, and the full quality escape lifecycle, and serves as CAMP's quality voice with OEMs, regulators, and key customers. The right candidate combines deep aviation maintenance knowledge with a disciplined, data-driven approach to compliance and continuous improvement.

This is a high-visibility leadership role reporting to the Vice President, Aviation Health Management Operations. The Director partners with senior leaders across a global organization and will build on an established quality program: strengthening the QMS, deepening OEM and customer confidence, and scaling quality practices as AHM grows.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Own and lead quality strategy across the full Aircraft Health Management organization, spanning maintenance tracking and engine health monitoring services, aligned with CAMP's business objectives.
* Serve as the escalation point for quality complaints from customer-facing, maintenance compliance, engine health monitoring, flight scheduling, and inventory functions.
* Partner with senior management and departmental leaders to embed quality methodologies across the organization and lead the associated change management.
* Own the quality budget, resource plan, and tooling (QMS, audit, and corrective action platforms), and build the succession pipeline for the quality team.

**Quality Management System & Certification**

* Own the Quality Management System (QMS) and quality SOPs, driving continuous improvement and ensuring processes meet strict regulatory and OEM requirements.
* Maintain ISO 9001 (or higher) certification for the engine health monitoring business, serving as external certification audit lead and ensuring ongoing audit readiness.
* Lead QMS management review with executive leadership, setting risk-based quality objectives and ensuring consistent QMS implementation (document control, competency records, data integrity) across all AHM locations in North America, Europe, and India.

**Audit & Compliance**

* Own the internal audit program end to end, including audit planning, execution, reporting, and the selection, training, and management of internal auditors.
* Host and manage OEM, customer, and third-party audits, driving findings to timely closure.

**Quality Escapes & Corrective Action**

* Manage all quality escapes from intake through investigation, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness, with clear accountability to customers and OEM partners.
* Define and report corrective action performance metrics (e.g., escape rate, time to containment, on-time closure, recurrence) with clear thresholds and escalation paths.

**OEM & Customer Engagement**

* Facilitate and chair weekly, monthly, and quarterly strategic OEM meetings covering quality trends, KPI compliance, and corrective action status.
* Serve as primary quality liaison to OEM partners, regulatory bodies, and high-profile customers and large fleet operators under significant OEM contracts.
* Facilitate weekly, monthly, and quarterly quality reviews with senior management and functional leaders, translating escape, audit, and customer feedback data into trends and strategic quality initiatives.

**Continuous Improvement & Team Leadership**

* Lead process improvement using Lean Six Sigma methods, mentoring teams and driving measurable reductions in escapes, rework, and risk.
* Maintain an executive quality scorecard (customer feedback, escapes, audit results, corrective action performance) to drive data-based decisions.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of four, setting priorities and fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and collaboration.
* Partner with AHM operations, training, and product leaders to ensure analyst competency, training effectiveness, and quality readiness for new products, processes, and teams.

 

**You have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum of 10 years of proven leadership experience in the aviation or aerospace sector, with senior quality assurance experience preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of aviation maintenance and its regulatory requirements (FAA, EASA, and OEM requirements). Hands-on aviation maintenance experience may offset formal credentials.
* Experience managing quality escapes, investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action programs.
* Experience owning or managing a QMS in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of ISO 9001 (AS9100 familiarity a plus).
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn quality data into executive-level metrics, insights, and recommendations.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships with OEMs, customers, and leaders at all levels of the organization.
* Strategic thinking with a strong focus on results and the ability to manage complex projects and initiatives.
* Ability to lead across a multi-site, multi-region team; willingness to travel to CAMP offices, OEM, and customer sites as needed.

**Nice to have:**

* Certified ISO 9001 Internal/External Auditor (or equivalent lead auditor certification) with hands-on audit experience.
* Six Sigma Black Belt, with demonstrated process improvement results.
* Quality manager certification (e.g., ASQ CQM) or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) is a bonus.
* Experience working with large OEM contracts and high-profile customers or large fleet operators.
* Experience in aircraft maintenance tracking, engine trend monitoring, or other SaaS/data-driven service environments.

 

**Why Work at CAMP?**

Join a culture where your ideas matter, your impact is real, and your growth is supported. Be part of a team reimagining the future of aviation.

CAMP is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer – vets/disabled

CAMP is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, please contact hr@campsystems.com (mailto:hr@campsystems.com).

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status EEO.

Equal Opportunity Employer

**Job Description:**

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Head of Global Quality Strategic Initiatives is responsible for defining, leading and executing enterprise-wide initiatives that strengthen TransMedics’ global quality management system (QMS), enhance regulatory compliance, improve product quality and patient safety, and advance operational excellence across the product lifecycle.

Partnering closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, this leader translates business priorities into measurable quality outcomes. The role drives complex transformation programs, anticipates emerging quality and regulatory risks, and establishes the processes, governance and metrics needed to support growth while maintaining high standards of safety, effectiveness and compliance.

The successful candidate combines deep medical device quality and regulatory expertise with strategic vision, strong business acumen and exceptional program leadership, with the ability to influence at every level of a global organization.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

This position is responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

* Develop and execute a multi-year global quality roadmap aligned with business priorities, regulatory expectations and patient safety. Identify systemic issues and emerging risks, prioritize transformation initiatives, and integrate quality priorities into business planning, product development and growth.
* Lead a portfolio of cross-functional quality programs with clear scope, milestones, resources, accountability and measurable outcomes. Establish executive steering committees, decision rights and escalation paths; resolve barriers, recommend investment priorities and track business impact and sustained results.
* Improve and harmonize the global QMS in line with FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, EU MDR and other applicable requirements. Strengthen process ownership, management review and effectiveness monitoring while accommodating regional requirements and local operating needs.
* Oversee improvement programs spanning document and records management, design and manufacturing controls, risk management, supplier quality, nonconformance, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), change control and post-market processes.
* Partner with Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders to assess regulatory changes and lead enterprise remediation programs addressing audit findings, regulatory observations and emerging risks. Support FDA inspections and external audits, resolve root causes, and embed sustainable inspection readiness.
* Define enterprise quality KPIs and key risk indicators covering CAPA effectiveness, complaints, nonconformances, audit findings, suppliers and product quality. Build consistent dashboards and executive reporting that improve visibility into risks, trends and program progress.
* Sponsor electronic QMS, quality data integration, advanced analytics and appropriate AI-enabled initiatives within applicable validation, privacy, security and regulatory controls. Promote data integrity, traceability and evidence-based decisions.
* Partner with functional leaders to strengthen product risk management, complaint handling, adverse event reporting, field action assessment and post-market monitoring from development and design transfer through manufacturing and post-market surveillance. Lead analysis of recurring issues and systemic failure modes to improve detection, containment and prevention.
* Apply Lean, Six Sigma and risk-based problem-solving to reduce rework, scrap, variation and the cost of poor quality while protecting compliance and patient safety. Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and site leaders to improve process capability and supplier performance, replicate best practices and measure benefits.
* Advise the Chief Regulatory Officer and executive leadership on quality priorities, systemic risks and transformation opportunities; communicate with the Board as appropriate. Influence priorities and resource decisions, mentor quality and program leaders, and lead training and change management that build accountability, transparency and lasting quality ownership.
* Collaborate with IT/Digital, Finance, Human Resources and other internal partners, and engage regulatory authorities, notified and certification bodies, external auditors, strategic suppliers, consultants and industry organizations as needed.
* Success will be measured by on-time transformation milestones; stronger QMS effectiveness and consistency; fewer recurring issues, overdue corrective actions and repeat audit findings; sustained inspection readiness; and measurable improvements in product quality, complaint trends, supplier performance and cost of poor quality.
* Perform other TransMedics tasks and duties as assigned.

**MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES**

Convene and lead cross-functional teams, establish program governance, and develop and mentor quality and program leaders within the approved mandate, budget and governance structure. Direct-report responsibilities are to be confirmed. Formal authority for regulatory decisions, product disposition, quality approvals and regulatory reporting remains with the accountable functions under company procedures.

**PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES**

This is an on-site role in Andover or Somerville, MA, with approximately 10–20% travel. Additional essential physical requirements, if applicable, are to be confirmed.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, Regulatory Affairs or a related technical discipline.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in medical devices, combination products or another highly regulated healthcare industry, including significant leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Affairs, quality transformation or enterprise program management.
* Proven success leading complex quality improvement, remediation or organizational change programs across business units, manufacturing sites and geographies, translating strategy into executable plans and measurable, sustainable results.
* Strong knowledge of FDA medical device requirements, including QMSR, and working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR and applicable global medical device frameworks.
* Hands-on experience with CAPA, nonconformances, complaints, design controls, supplier quality, change management, audits, remediation and post-market surveillance; understanding of root cause analysis, process validation, manufacturing controls and QMS effectiveness.
* Familiarity with electronic QMS platforms, quality data analytics and computerized system validation or assurance (CSV/CSA) principles.
* Ability to influence senior executives and stakeholders in a global matrix organization, communicate complex issues clearly, and drive decisions without relying on direct authority.
* Demonstrated strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving, change leadership and talent development, with sound risk-based judgment, integrity and accountability for product quality, patient safety and regulatory compliance.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Business Administration or a related field.
* Professional certifications in quality (ASQ CQE or CMQ/OE), regulatory affairs (RAC), program management (PMP), Lean Six Sigma or change management.
* Experience with MasterControl.

As part of our long-term growth plans, TransMedics is excited to announce our plan to relocate our headquarters (HQ) to Somerville, MA by 2028. We chose this location because we believe it is a place where innovation will thrive. Our new state-of-the-art headquarters is designed to support collaboration, creativity, and discovery. We believe this will be a place where we can continue to do things few thought possible in organ transplantation to help patients. *Specific timing and role impact may vary.*

TransMedics, Inc. is a commercial-stage medical technology company transforming organ transplant therapy for patients worldwide. Our mission is to help save more patients’ lives by increasing access to viable donor organs for those who are awaiting an organ transplant. To accomplish this mission, we partner closely with transplant stakeholders worldwide and help expand their access to healthy donor organs, while delivering the highest quality technology, service, clinical care and outcomes. 
 
Driven by a passion for improving patient care, we make the impossible possible and keep our employees at the center of everything we do. Together, we strive to enhance the quality of life for transplant recipients and their families, fostering hope and healing in the journey toward better health. 
 
**Maximize your potential at TransMedics, Inc.** 
www.TransMedics.com

TransMedics is committed to equitable and transparent compensation. The expected base salary range for this role is $232,800-$331,350, which represents the company’s current good-faith estimate of compensation for this position. Actual salary will depend on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and the specific work location. This role may also be eligible for bonuses, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, retirement savings, paid time off, and wellness resources). We comply with all U.S. pay transparency laws and do not request or consider salary history.

Medical with Health Reimbursement Account through Blue Cross/Blue Shield of MA

Dental

Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account

Short Term Disability

Long Term Disability

401K Plan

Employee Stock Purchase Plan

card.description:
**Job Description:**

**Position Overview**
---------------------

TransMedics is seeking a **Senior Director of Automation and New Process Engineering** to lead a critical transformation within our R&D and Engineering organization. This highly visible leadership position will oversee Automation, New Product Introduction (NPI), and Sustaining Engineering, driving engineering innovation, manufacturing excellence, and operational scalability.

**This is a build role, not a maintain role.**

As TransMedics continues its rapid growth, we need a strategic, hands-on engineering leader who can develop and execute a multi-year transformation roadmap while remaining closely connected to day-to-day manufacturing operations.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in automation and advanced manufacturing with proven experience building high-performing engineering organizations. This leader will drive improvements in product quality, reliability, manufacturing efficiency, and scalability while developing the engineering talent needed to support our continued growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

**Engineering Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Lead the Automation, New Product Introduction, and Sustaining Engineering organizations.
* Develop and execute a multi-year engineering transformation strategy aligned with business growth.
* Build, mentor, and develop high-performing, multidisciplinary engineering teams.
* Establish organizational structures, processes, and capabilities to support long-term scalability.
* Oversee performance management, professional development, and engineering resource planning.

**Automation & Advanced Manufacturing**

* Drive the implementation of advanced automation, robotics, and innovative manufacturing technologies.
* Lead automation initiatives across multiple manufacturing lines to improve quality, efficiency, and throughput.
* Identify opportunities to modernize manufacturing processes, systems, and infrastructure.
* Establish scalable, reliable, and cost-effective manufacturing solutions.

**New Product Introduction & Sustaining Engineering**

* Provide strategic leadership for NPI engineering and manufacturing process development.
* Ensure successful transitions from product development into scalable manufacturing.
* Lead sustaining engineering initiatives to improve existing products and manufacturing processes.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to resolve complex technical challenges and support product launches.
* Maintain a hands-on approach to troubleshooting manufacturing issues and addressing production or launch risks.

**Design for Excellence (DfX)**

* Champion Design for Excellence (DfX), including Design for Manufacturability (DFM), throughout the product development lifecycle.
* Drive product and process simplification, including part-count reduction.
* Improve product reliability, manufacturing efficiency, and cost effectiveness through engineering design improvements.
* Establish best practices supporting consistent, scalable manufacturing performance.

**Strategic Collaboration & Operational Excellence**

* Partner closely with R&D, Quality, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing leadership.
* Drive continuous improvement in engineering systems, processes, and infrastructure.
* Leverage manufacturing technologies, digital tools, and operational data to improve engineering outcomes.
* Support capital planning, resource allocation, and strategic investment decisions.
* Foster a culture of technical excellence, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications**
------------------

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
* 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience specifying, developing, and implementing automation across multiple manufacturing lines.
* Strong technical understanding of manufacturing processes, automation technologies, and engineering operations.
* Ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on technical problem-solving.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* MBA or advanced degree.
* Proven success leading multidisciplinary engineering organizations through significant growth or transformation.
* Experience implementing advanced manufacturing technologies, including robotics and automated production systems.
* Strong understanding of Design for Excellence (DfX) and Design for Manufacturability (DFM).
* Knowledge of regulatory frameworks, quality systems, and compliance requirements.
* Experience leveraging Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and digital manufacturing technologies.
* Demonstrated financial acumen, capital planning, project management, and resource allocation experience.
* Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain exceptional engineering talent.

**Work Environment**
--------------------

This position operates in both office and manufacturing floor environments and requires a leader who is comfortable engaging directly with engineering teams, manufacturing operations, and cross-functional stakeholders.

**Compensation & Benefits**
---------------------------

TransMedics is committed to equitable and transparent compensation.

The expected base salary range for this position is **$220,600 – $314,050 annually**, representing the company's current good-faith estimate of compensation.

Actual compensation will depend on factors including candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and specific work location.

This position may also be eligible for:

* Performance-based bonuses
* Equity compensation
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Retirement savings benefits
* Paid time off
* Wellness resources

TransMedics complies with all applicable U.S. pay transparency laws and does not request or consider salary history.

**About TransMedics**
---------------------

TransMedics is transforming organ transplantation through innovative technologies designed to improve the availability, utilization, and outcomes of donor organs.

Our mission is to help save more lives by advancing the science and technology of organ preservation and transplantation.

Join a growing organization where engineering innovation, technical excellence, and meaningful impact come together to advance life-saving technology.

This is a full-time, **on-site position** currently based at TransMedics' facility in Andover, MA.

TransMedics is preparing to transition operations to a new facility in **Somerville, MA**. Candidates should be aware of this upcoming move and must be willing and able to work on-site at both locations as the transition occurs.

Candidates must currently reside within commuting distance of the work location or be willing to relocate to the Greater Boston area.

This position requires regular collaboration with engineering, manufacturing, and cross-functional teams, including direct engagement on the manufacturing floor.

TransMedics is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

TransMedics is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and hiring process.

We value the unique perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences of our employees and believe that an inclusive workforce strengthens our ability to innovate and fulfill our mission of saving lives.
